options: The job record itself (name and metadata) — with no steps yet
A fully scheduled, ready-to-run job with default steps
An operator to notify on failure
A backup schedule
questions.explain: sp_add_job creates only the job shell; sp_add_jobstep is what gives it something to actually do.

questions.q: Which stored procedure attaches a T-SQL command (or other subsystem) to a job as a step?
options: sp_add_jobstep
sp_add_job
sp_add_schedule
sp_add_jobserver
questions.explain: sp_add_jobstep defines the subsystem (e.g. TSQL), the command, and the database context for that step.

questions.q: Why are schedules created with sp_add_schedule as separate objects rather than embedded directly in a job?
options: So one schedule can be attached to multiple jobs via sp_attach_schedule
Because msdb doesn't allow storing a schedule inside a job record
Because schedules must be created through SSMS, never T-SQL
So the schedule can be encrypted separately from the job
questions.explain: Schedules are independent objects; sp_attach_schedule links a schedule to one or more jobs, letting a maintenance window drive several jobs at once.

questions.q: A job has steps and an attached schedule but never actually runs. What's the most likely missing piece?
options: sp_add_jobserver was never run to target the job at a server
The job needs a second step
msdb needs to be restarted
The schedule's @freq_type is invalid and silently ignored
questions.explain: Without sp_add_jobserver, the job isn't assigned to run on any server — it exists but never fires, a very common oversight.

questions.q: In sp_add_jobstep, what does @subsystem = N'TSQL' specify?
options: That the step's command is executed as T-SQL rather than another subsystem like PowerShell or SSIS
That the job runs against the tempdb system database only
That the step uses two-phase commit
That the step is disabled by default
questions.explain: @subsystem tells Agent how to interpret @command — TSQL for a T-SQL batch, but other values run PowerShell, SSIS packages, CmdExec, and more.
